title: Type Hints & Dataclasses
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Type Hints & Dataclasses in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Type hint
items.text: A type hint documents the type a variable, parameter or return value is expected to use.

items.heading: Parameter hint
items.text: A function parameter can include a type hint after its name.

items.heading: Return hint
items.text: A return annotation documents the expected return type.
items.code: def add(a: int, b: int) -> int: ...

items.heading: Tooling benefit
items.text: Type hints improve readability and help editors, linters and type checkers understand code.

items.heading: Runtime enforcement
items.text: Python does not automatically enforce normal type hints at runtime. They are mainly annotations unless extra checking is used.

items.heading: Union with |
items.text: Modern Python can use | to indicate that a value may have more than one type.

items.heading: Generic types
items.text: Generic types describe the type of items inside a container or the parameters of a reusable type.

items.heading: Dataclass
items.text: A dataclass is a convenient way to define classes mainly used to store data.

items.heading: @dataclass
items.text: The dataclass decorator can generate common methods and reduce repetitive class boilerplate.

items.heading: Dataclass field
items.text: A field is a declared piece of data stored by a dataclass instance.

items.heading: Useful annotations
items.text: Good type hints should describe the real intended data and remain understandable to the people maintaining the code.
